column2: Tony Silva
column3: claiming Silva violated the state’s ethics code when he failed to disclose his financial interest in a controversial wetlands property in Cumberland.

column1: The state GOP is filing the complaint with the R.I. Ethics Commission
column2: accusing the governor’s top aide of not disclosing his financial ties to the 45 Canning St. property between 2017 and 2020. The complaint comes one day after Target 12 first reported Silva directly intervened with the Cumberland mayor earlier this year in an effort to get the controversial wetlands property developed
column3: long after he claimed he no longer had a financial interest in the lot.

column1: “Although Mr. Silva admits he had a financial interest in the 45 Canning Street [lot] from 2017 through 2020
column2: in financial disclosure reports for that time period
column3: Mr. Silva never disclosed he had a financial interest in 45 Canning Street property
column4: ” Republican leaders wrote in a news release.

column1: The group pointed to a state law that requires certain public officials to regularly disclose their financial activities
column2: including “a listing of all real property in which a financial interest was held.”

column1: Silva had been trying to develop the property since 2017 when he received an option to buy it if regulatory permits for development were obtained. The R.I. Department of Environmental Management initially rejected permit requests in 2019
column2: but reversed that decision this year. Development of the wetlands property has been opposed by neighbors and the town for years.

column1: Silva claims he transferred his financial interest in the property to his son
column2: Ross Silva
column3: in April 2020
column4: saying has documentation to prove it
column5: although he hasn’t yet provided it.

column1: As the top aide to McKee since the start of 2015
column2: Silva is required to annually disclose his financial interests in various properties and business ventures. A Target 12 review of Silva’s disclosure forms between 2017 and 2020 shows no mention of the property at 45 Canning St. (In 2019
column3: he did list a financial interest in a property on the same road
column4: at 114 Canning St.)

column1: In addition to the ethics complaint
column2: the GOP is calling on R.I. Attorney General Peter Neronha to investigate Silva’s decision to try and influence development of the property. New documents released under an Access to Public Records Act request show Silva asked to meet with with Cumberland officials regarding the development last September
column3: months after he supposedly gave up any financial interest in the project.

column1: This past March
column2: the month Silva became chief of staff in the governor’s office
column3: he asked Cumberland Mayor Jeff Mutter for an unscheduled meeting
column4: and the mayor claims Silva asked him not to oppose the Canning Street development.

column1: In a text to the mayor afterward
column2: Silva indicated he had spoken to his wife and they were “going to allow my son Ross” to buy the lot.

column1: “Therefore I won’t be connected to it at all at the time of sale
column2: ” Silva wrote. “Hopefully this will make it easier for you at Town Hall.”

column1: Silva’s son bought the property in July
column2: which he has since said he will donate to the town. The governor’s chief of staff nonetheless has denied he tried to influence the deal in any way.

column1: “I want to emphasize that at no time did I intervene on my behalf or anyone else regarding the property
column2: ” Silva wrote Monday to Target 12. “NEVER EVER.”
